result.title: Passable for Whom? Few-Shot Personal Calibration of Sidewalk Accessibility Perception
result.summary: Whether a sidewalk is passable depends on who is trying to pass: people who use the same mobility aid disagree about the same image, so one label per scene, or per aid, is wrong for many of them. We introduce few-shot personal accessibility perception: from K answers of a person never seen before, predict their judgment of sidewalk scenes never seen before. PassCal separates a shared description of the scene from the person's interpretation of it. The description comes from the internal state of a frozen vision-language model (VLM) and from barrier type, severity and context properties predicted by a detector trained on 14.9k public audits; the interpretation, a calibration of the person's response style and a weighting of the properties, is fit from their answers. On 8,883 judgments in which each of 135 verified mobility-aid users rated the same 50 sidewalk scenes, with people and scenes both held out, eight answers lower the Brier score from 0.550 to 0.479. The same VLM prompted with those answers reaches 0.562, and the same calibration without the scene 0.521. Conformal risk control turns predictions into passable, blocked or "depends on you" statements with a bounded expected rate of wrong statements over people; at 5%, eight answers raise the share of decisive scenes from 27% to 42%. Audit-supervised properties improve all sixteen vision and VLM encoders we test and outperform attributes from a sidewalk navigation VLM.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 few-shot 个人化人行道可通行性预测任务与 PassCal：以冻结 VLM 的内部状态加检测器给出的障碍类型、严重度与情境属性构成共享场景描述，再用个人少量回答拟合其作答风格与属性权重，并用 conformal risk control 输出「可通行／受阻／取决于你」三类判定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把冻结 VLM 内部状态当作显式场景描述、再单独校准「个人如何解读」的分解，可供核查 latent 表示中的内容与使用方式能否分离；保形风险控制约束误判率的三类判定，也可能为 LVR 的停止／弃答决策提供借鉴，但原文未涉及 latent 推理的生成与更新。
